Support for parallel computing

Source: R/RcppExports.R, R/parallel.R
parallel.Rd

The dqrng package provides several fast random number generators that are suited for parallel usage. The function dqrng_advance_stream allows to switch the RNG to a different (sub)stream. Note that substream handling via the option use_substream is only available for the Xoshiro256+/++/**, MWC192X, and Threefry generators.

The dqclusterRNGStream function prepares a parallel-type cluster for reproducible random number generation.

dqrng_advance_stream(stream, use_substream = FALSE)

dqclusterSetRNGStream(cl = NULL, use_substream = FALSE, register = TRUE)

Arguments

stream

integer used for selecting the RNG stream; either a scalar or a vector of length 2

use_substream

Use different substreams instead of different streams

cl

parallel-type cluster

register

Should the RNG be registered as user-defined, default TRUE

See also

clusterSetRNGStream and makeCluster

Examples

library("dqrng")
# get some random numbers
dqset.seed(123456) 
cl <- parallel::makePSOCKcluster(2)
dqclusterSetRNGStream(cl)
r1 <- parallel::clusterApply(cl, rep(3, 2), dqrng::dqrunif)
parallel::stopCluster(cl)
# do the same again
dqset.seed(123456) 
cl <- parallel::makePSOCKcluster(2)
dqclusterSetRNGStream(cl)
r2 <- parallel::clusterApply(cl, rep(3, 2), dqrng::dqrunif)
parallel::stopCluster(cl)
# make sure results are equal
all.equal(r1, r2)
#> [1] TRUE
